The **People's Vanguard Party** ([Arabic]: حزب الطليعة الشعبية), also referred to as **at-Tali'a**,[[1]]#cite_note-1) was a [Ba'athist] political party in [Yemen].[[2]]#cite_note-ta-2)[[3]]#cite_note-3) The party was established in the late 1950s.[[4]]#cite_note-nbr-4) It was the Yemeni branch of the [Baath Party]. When the Baath Party was divided between Syrian and Iraqi factions, the Yemeni branch overwhelmingly sided with the Syrian-led Ba'ath Party.[[5]]#cite_note-hidi-5)[[4]]#cite_note-nbr-4)[[6]]#cite_note-6) After the split, the Syrian-aligned Ba'athists 'Yemenized' their party and took the name People's Vanguard Party.[[5]]#cite_note-hidi-5)

[![Image 4]]

The Third Conference of the People's Vanguard Party

The members of the party were largely recruited from teachers, students, and intellectuals.[[4]]#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was based in [Aden], and had limited presence outside the city.[[4]]#cite_note-nbr-4) It had some presence in Hadhramaut for a brief period.[[4]]#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was banned in [North Yemen], where it was part of the [National Democratic Front] "National Democratic Front (Yemen)") and took part in the [NDF Rebellion].[[5]]#cite_note-hidi-5)

The party was one of two non-[National Front] "National Liberation Front (South Yemen)") (NF) parties tolerated during the early 1970s. In October 1975 it joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization of the National Front[[7]]#cite_note-Hobday-7) (which evolved into the [Yemeni Socialist Party] in 1978).[[2]]#cite_note-ta-2) The merger was ratified by the third PVP congress held in August 1975.[[8]]#cite_note-8)
